rows.name: Handwritten note, held
rows.what: A hand holds a small handwritten note to camera beside the product, shallow focus, real surface. The claim is entirely in the handwriting.
rows.why_it_works: Handwriting reads as a person, not a brand, so the claim lands before the defence goes up. Cheapest shape in the bank — no model, no studio, no retouching.
rows.evidence: duplicated ×4 in the sample, across two different copy blocks

carries: a rejection of the expensive alternative

rows.name: UGC post, screenshotted
rows.what: A real woman at her mirror or holding her phone, shot as if it were her own post, with review cards or step panels laid over it. Often framed as a phone screen.
rows.why_it_works: It is the closest thing in the paid set to what she already scrolls. The ad borrows the shape of organic content rather than interrupting it.

rows.name: Struck price
rows.what: Old price struck through, new price beside it, usually circled or in a pill. Product and little else.
rows.why_it_works: Does one job with no argument at all, which is why it survives being run at volume alongside everything else.
rows.evidence: duplicated ×6 in the sample — the most repeated treatment overall, though it is an offer shape not an argument shape

rows.name: Split with data labels
rows.what: Two macro images side by side, each with one hard label in a black pill — a number, a name, a state. No sentence.
rows.why_it_works: Asserts a difference without claiming a result, so it reads as information rather than advertising and survives review.
rows.evidence: duplicated ×3 in the Froya science block

rows.name: Red-circle annotation
rows.what: A photograph with a hand-drawn red ellipse around the thing being pointed at, usually with a short pointer label.
rows.why_it_works: The most recognisable 'look here' mark there is, borrowed from evidence rather than advertising.
rows.evidence: duplicated across BOTH advertisers — 4+ in the Froya science block, plus before/after use in <competitor>

rows.name: Phone notes list
rows.what: A screenshot of the notes app: lowercase title, then five or six em-dash lines. No photography at all.
rows.why_it_works: Reads as something she wrote for herself. A list carries six objections in one ad without feeling like a feature list.

carries: an accumulated list of failed fixes

rows.name: Hand-annotated product
rows.what: The product on a plain ground with pencil arrows and handwritten notes pointing at parts of it.
rows.why_it_works: Same trick as the sticky note at spec-sheet scale — handwriting makes a claim list feel like a person explaining rather than a brand listing.

carries: the whole offer in one frame

rows.name: Annotated diagram
rows.what: A medical or technical illustration with leader lines to labelled parts, in textbook language rather than brand language.
rows.why_it_works: Borrows the authority of the reference book, and carries a mechanism with no person in frame — so no casting problem.
rows.evidence: duplicated ×2, plus near-relatives (histology grid, molecular render) in the same block

rows.name: Editorial page
rows.what: Laid out as a magazine or news page — masthead, standfirst, a highlighted passage — with the product inside the article.
rows.why_it_works: Arrives as journalism. It is the static version of the advertorial the account already runs its winner through.

rows.name: Study figure
rows.what: An actual scientific chart — axes, error bars, significance stars — with one result circled.
rows.why_it_works: The only shape in the set that looks like it was not made for the ad.
rows.evidence: duplicated ×2 in the Froya science block

carries: a mechanism with a real citation behind it

rows.name: Shot in the shop
rows.what: Documentary photograph at a counter or shelf — real lighting, real staff, nothing styled.
rows.why_it_works: Reads as a photograph somebody took, not a set that was built. Strong pairing with the native long-form play.

rows.name: Us versus the shelf
rows.what: Their whole category on one side — a wall of competing bottles — and one product on the other.
rows.why_it_works: Turns the number of things she has already tried into the argument.

carries: an accumulated list of failed fixes

rows.name: Annotated face
rows.what: One face, split or part-treated, with small callout labels naming each side and a headline in her voice.

rows.name: Selfie with a review pinned
rows.what: A real unretouched selfie with a single review card floating over it.

rows.name: Review cluster
rows.what: Three or four review cards scattered over a plain ground with one aggregate line under them.

rows.name: Comment plus number
rows.what: A screenshotted comment pinned top-left, one very large percentage under it, and the panel it came from named.
rows.evidence: observed ×1, with a big-number-plus-model variant in a second block

carries: a claim that needs a denominator

rows.name: Editorial essay card
rows.what: A quiet interior photograph, a serif headline and three short paragraphs — a magazine page, not an ad.

rows.name: Spec callouts
rows.what: Product dead centre on white, five or six benefit labels radiating on thin leader lines.

carries: the whole offer in one frame

rows.name: A/B question
rows.what: A single face split down the middle with a literal question and two buttons under it.

carries: a demonstration that invites a reply

rows.name: Enemy headline
rows.what: Heavy condensed type on black naming the thing that failed her, product small and low in frame.
rows.evidence: observed ×1, but it opens the most-duplicated Froya block

rows.name: Split face with a study claim
rows.what: A face split down the middle on black, with a percentage claim set across it.

rows.name: Scan comparison
rows.what: Two ultrasound or microscopy frames side by side, red circles on the difference, timeframes labelled.
rows.evidence: observed ×2 in the Froya science block

rows.name: Dark benefit stack
rows.what: Three or four benefit rows stacked over a dark, moody product photograph.

carries: the whole offer in one frame

rows.name: Borrowed authority
rows.what: The product in the hands of someone whose uniform does the arguing.

rows.name: Big number
rows.what: The discount at enormous scale, product clustered under it.
rows.evidence: duplicated ×8 in the Froya clearance block — the single most repeated shape in that advertiser's set
